title: A Neuron Must Work to Die

scenes.tts: Take away nerve growth factor, N G F, from a young sympathetic neuron in a dish. It dies within a day or two. Now add a drug that stops it making new proteins. The death is delayed. That is strange, because a starving cell should run down faster. Instead, the neuron has to make something in order to die.

scenes.tts: So dying is a program, and a worm revealed its parts. In a transparent worm, the same named cells die on schedule in every animal. Two genes, C E D three and C E D four, are needed for these deaths. Without them, the cells live. Lose a third gene, C E D nine, and cells that should live die. Remove C E D three or C E D four as well, and those deaths stop.
scenes.caption: So dying is a program, and a worm revealed its parts. In a transparent worm, the same named cells die on schedule in every animal. scenes.visual: A lineage tree whose branch ends die or live; ced-3 and ced-4 chips drive the deaths; ced-9 brakes them; the tree responds to each loss.

scenes.tts: Cloning connected the worm to mammals. C E D three encodes a protein similar to a protease, of the family later named caspases. C E D four is related to a mammalian protein, Apaf one. C E D nine encodes a relative of Bcl two, a protein that keeps cells alive. The match is imperfect. The worm has no clear counterpart of Bax.

The match is imperfect. The worm has no clear counterpart of Bax.

scenes.tts: Now return to the neuron without N G F. Its survival signal falls. A stress pathway turns on, and a protein called c-Jun rises. Pro-death relatives of Bcl two are made. This is the new gene expression that the drug blocked. Bax is needed for cytochrome c to leave the mitochondria.

scenes.visual: A chain of chips falls into place from the lost NGF signal to c-Jun and Bim; a mitochondrion full of cytochrome c opens a gap when Bax arrives and the dots leave.

scenes.tts: In the cytoplasm, cytochrome c binds Apaf one. Apaf one assembles into a wheel called the apoptosome. The apoptosome activates caspase nine, which cuts and activates caspase three. Executioner caspases dismantle the cell. They also expose an eat me signal on its surface.
scenes.caption: In the cytoplasm, cytochrome c binds Apaf-1. Apaf-1 assembles into a wheel called the apoptosome. The apoptosome activates caspase-9, which cuts and activates caspase-3. Executioner caspases dismantle the cell. They also expose an "eat me" signal on its surface.
scenes.visual: Cytochrome c dots bind Apaf-1 pieces that close into a wheel; caspase-9 then caspase-3 light up; the cell shrinks and an eat-me tag appears.
scenes.narration: In the cytoplasm, cytochrome c binds Apaf-1. Apaf-1 assembles into a wheel called the apoptosome. The apoptosome activates caspase-9, which cuts and activates caspase-3. Executioner caspases dismantle the cell. They also expose an "eat me" signal on its surface.

scenes.tts: Is that the only step N G F controls? Researchers injected cytochrome c into neurons kept in N G F. The neurons survived. Neurons deprived of N G F for about fifteen to twenty hours died after the injection, and a caspase inhibitor prevented their death. So N G F holds the death program back at more than one step. Death is a program, held back at more than one step.
